entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Canachus the Younger (b. 500 BCE, Sicyon) was a renowned musician and composer of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Sicyon. Known for his contributions to the fields of painters and sculptors.

As a prominent figure in the artistic circles of Sicyon, Canachus the Younger collaborated with other notable artists, including the famous painter Pheidias, who created the iconic statue of Zeus at Olympia. This collaboration reflects the cultural exchange and innovation that characterized the Classical period.

Canachus the Younger's legacy extends beyond his own time, as his compositions and artistic theories influenced the development of Western music and art. His work continues to be studied and performed by scholars and artists today.

In a striking example of the enduring impact of Classical art, a fragment of Canachus the Younger's composition 'Hymn to Apollo' was discovered in 2010, dating back to the 5th century BCE. This find sheds new light on the artistic practices and cultural values of the ancient Greeks.
